body:
Currently listed AnimatedTexture Issues:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/89972 - No longer prints errors on this branch, but does not 'behave'
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/87312 - Resolved by this PR
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/79070 - Resolved by this PR
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70090 - Appears to have been resolved before this build. Tested on 4.6 on my Mac
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/54506 - Not resolved, but would be as a side effect of using DrawableTextures + https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115653
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/77415 & https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/69621 are both derived from Editor trying to save redraws. Could be resolved, but that might not be desirable.
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/44625 - Not resolved, primarily intentional behavior.

Some more of these could hypothetically be resolved as part of this refactor, but come with tradeoffs and questions.
* AnimatedTextures can appear 'stuttery' in the editor because the animation is subscribed to RenderingServer frame_pre_draw, and the Editor tries to skip drawing new frames when possible for processor usage. This is hypothetically resolvable, but would also mean the Editor is forced to update continuously when an AnimatedTexture is on screen
* AnimatedTextures, being resources, exist outside of the scene tree, and thus will continue to animate on 'paused' nodes. The resource has an independent pause variable, which is exposed and accessible. Also hypothetically resolvable, by subscribing the set_pause function on the resource to the process modes on Nodes that own the Texture, but could introduce conflicts where two Nodes 'argue' over whether the texture should be paused.

Extra note on stuttery editor, see:  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/113224
Extra note on un-pausable animations: the same is currently true for AnimatedTiles, which use "AnimationSlice" commands for the Rendering Device, and cannot be paused.

Extra Note 3: I'm not 100% sure using the DrawableTextures API & Shaders is even necessary? There are other ways to update the data inside a texture, via Copy_effects, or https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109985 - Probably worth a test.

Extra Note 4: I'm guessing MipMaps are not desirable for AnimatedTextures, but that could be adjusted. Would introduce a little more tax per redraw, redrawing all mipmaps

> This is hypothetically resolvable, but would also mean the Editor is forced to update continuously when an AnimatedTexture is on screen

This is fine, as long as the redraw is not forced when the animated texture is invisible.

Pushed a new build of this refactor.

> AnimatedTextures can appear 'stuttery' in the editor because the animation is subscribed to RenderingServer frame_pre_draw, and the Editor tries to skip drawing new frames when possible for processor usage. This is hypothetically resolvable, but would also mean the Editor is forced to update continuously when an AnimatedTexture is on screen
> Kobewi: This is fine, as long as the redraw is not forced when the animated texture is invisible.

Resolves:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/77415
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/69621

To resolve stutter in Editor, AnimatedTextures now also add an empty 'AnimationSlice' rendering command to their CanvasItem - this will trigger a redraw request whenever the CanvasItem is visible. This resolves most stutter, but derived uses of an AnimatedTexture (such as using it as the Albedo in a material) still do not have enough info to force redraw when visible.

In investigating this, I found that the RenderingServer API `texture_set_redraw_if_visible` appears totally defunct, and does not link to any behaviors. With permission, I'll remove it along with this refactor. The function was only invoked in this class and is essentially unimplemented in both backends.
Rebased to Master as of July 16th. Verified nothing broke.
